title: Am I the only one who enjoyed AI game development because of the lack of human interaction?
author: FrevealD
selftext: Of course, games are made for human beings, so real feedback is needed (my poor wife felt obliged to play my game every day). But did you actually enjoy being able to work with AI instead of a bunch of people, without having discussions about discussions? For me, the most satisfying part was that I could focus on the task without drama, "just" with the sycophancy I had to overcome. How do you feel about it? Any other sociopaths like me?

comments.author: Junior_Air_3329
comments.body: I haven’t even began with the ai yet. But. Yes.

comments.author: qualiadev
comments.body:
Dude after this last year of battling people to get features prioritized I knew was necessary, just being able to make things without having to go through product or legal or management has been the most therapeutic thing.

And I have my agent not just agree with everything too, but yeah it’s been so much fun. At some point I need the human testers though

comments.author: Relevant-Positive-48
comments.body:
I've worked on professional and indie games before and after AI got useful and no.  I honestly wish more people doing indie work with AI would do it in small teams.  Solo developing is fun but working with a team that's actually aligned on vision is magical.    
  
I'd like to see something like musical band setups where you've got 3-5 people covering the disciplines (sometimes doubling up and sometimes having more than one on something)

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body: a team would be cool but no one i know has the same passion for my project as i do so i dont really have much of a choice.

replies.author: Relevant-Positive-48
replies.body:
That's because you're thinking everyone aligned on vision needs to be as passionate about the "project" as you.  They only need to be as passionate about their piece of the project as you are about the project as a whole.  

An artist, for example, might find your project perfect for their style.

replies.author: Timely_Spirit_9053
replies.body: Maybe but good luck finding an artist willing to put in time for free, i dont have money to hire people when im working on a free game

replies.author: Specialist_Top_6079
replies.body: The chances of getting a team aligned with the same vision, without paying them is next to nil.

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: Yes, right there with you. No boss overhead going “this is what’s hot, put this in here” none of the bullshit corporate fools who haven’t touched a game in their lives tell me what is best for the genre. It’s absolutely an important part of this.

comments.author: delicious_pubes
comments.body:
In a fantasy world where my game makes good money I would invest in a small team of experts. I have professional experience in technical game design and narrative but not in animation, modeling, rendering or many other disciplines that would elevate my projects. 

I don’t see a lot of the highest quality work shared on Reddit, but at my job I see what domain experts can do with the tools and it’s a whole other level.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: for the most part, yes. That's one of the things I like most. But I also like working with a small team of like-minded people, so I'm currently working with a partner I've worked with for a decade and we both use AI and improve the game with our own sensibilities, but we trust each other so it's a good working relationship

comments.author: mrpoopistan
comments.body: You need to find better people if you don't enjoy working with people.

replies.author: brightfutureman
replies.body:
The problem is they are very expensive and you can’t start with the best one as you simply don’t have such a budget.

But the thing is that Claude is much more better than average Joe in thinking and proposing things when you stuck. It’s like making conversation with the smarter person than yourself. Which is mostly very helpful. And of course for low budget - you won’t find a smart person to work on you/with you. Plus a lot of problem with their and mine ego. Frictions in vision. Laziness. Waiting. Meh… Claude is my best partner at this moment.

comments.author: Sakcrel
comments.body: 100% I love not having to wait hours, if not days, for someone to answer my problem in a forum or having to deal with an artist delay my commission for the fourth time.

comments.author: AutomaticTalent
comments.body:
I’ve been a game producer 1987-2017 and worked on literally over 100 games with teams of up to 20+ people and I felt EXACTLY the same when I used AI to develop my own game alone.

Took 4 months and came out exactly like I designed it.

Previously it would have taken that much time to design, plan development, build the team - then at LEAST six more months to get it up and running.

I really did enjoy not having to coddle and cajole each discipline to do their planning, scheduling, come to work on time, meet their deadlines.

I have a picture of our daily AM meeting where a 10+ person team is sitting around the meeting table and ALL are looking down at open laptops while I was conducting it.

The message was “this meeting is useless so I’ll just ‘work’ during this meeting” - as they browsed the net.

I know development planning meetings are boring but if they just focused we could all get back to the work.

It was truly a pleasure to work alone with AI handling coding and most art tasks which allowed me to focus on design, audio, QA, and debugging.

replies.author: Shrineheart
replies.body:
This. I'm making a game with the help of AI and I've tried talking with programmers and dev groups before. But projects were aimless or not well thought out, or I couldn't properly explain what I was trying to make.

I'm an artist and I'm making all the art for my game. I think in art terms. I'm visual. I was starting to go crazy trying to explain the game design to programmers and feeling discouraged... Then I built part of it myself. Then I started discussing my project with AI and found a dev partner that doesn't hear me rattle off my ideas and go "that's too complicated" or "are you sure this isn't scope creep?".

The thing everyone always seems to miss is that I have to think about the finished game. Everything in it. What does this game look like when the player has put all the hours in and unlocked everything? For some reason everyone thinks I mean "I have to have the first prototype have everything." I'm not crazy, I know it's built in parts lol

It's hard to find people who are invested in working on a project that's big, especially if you can't pay (and I don't blame people especially these days!). If there's no interest then there's no incentive.

Sitting down with AI in little sessions for months helped organize all of my scattered rambling notes and nail down decisions I needed to finalize. Now, development is flying. It's still going to take time and a lot of pixel art and writing and sound design on my part but not having to get frustrated about not being understood or being talked over is just so, so freeing. I can make something that looks like what I want and plays well. 

My game has a lot of customization and accessibility features. I planned these from the start and I had people act like that wasn't something I should prioritize right off the bat. But setting it up that way has made so much stuff possible and made things a lot easier on me as the project artist. I don't have to sit there during a meeting arguing that "Yes, prosthetics should be in the game" or "No, we're not defaulting to 6 desaturated skintones and 5 hairstyles." I can go "this is what I have planned visually. Let's make it work in the smoothest way possible." And we just... Go! It's great!

I would love to one day work with a team. But I'd need to find the right people. And I'm tired of waiting to make this in hopes that someday maybe I'll find a team I mesh with.

With AI I can make it now.

comments.author: DealerIcy3439
comments.body: Would be nice to get an extra hand on a project but till someday a mysterious person wants to agree to work together, in a solo wether I wanna be it or not. Having a partner would be nice tho. I just know it won’t happen for me, I’m also very cautious sharing my game vision anywhere due to any possible copycats. Still designing the map and it’s taking a while

comments.author: affabledrunk
comments.body: People suck, man, its all egos and issues. Ive been workig as real engineer for 30 years and its always a fucking drama with half the people. They don't undestand. they have poliical issues, they don't like you, they're lazy and on and on. Its such a frictionless pleasure to work with AI, its everything that collaboration should be.

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body: I wish i had a team of people to help. unfortunately people dont work for free and i have no treasure. and I refuse to do the whole equity thing because I think its wrong to offer the whole, oh you get some money when its done crap because then they are all teh time worried while working that things might not work out or that things will fall through at the end.

comments.author: LaidBackDev
comments.body: This sound sad out of context.

comments.author: Amazing_Strawberry70
comments.body: Human interaction can be dramaless, you just have to find that kind of people.

comments.author: caesium23
comments.body: I would be shocked if a significant portion of AI devs aren't neurodivergent of some kind.

comments.author: viral-architect
comments.body: I never made games until now. It's fun when you don't have people breathing down your neck the whole time.
